messages.body_plain:
Dear Vincent

I am also getting a similar error ("Error in if (is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuider)) { : argument is of length zero") with GGIR v3.1-2 and v3.1-5 when processing data files that were collected during the change of daylight savings. I was able to proceed with the analysis by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()) as suggested by Grace. Attached are the milestone data for a few data files to assist with the investigation.

Thank you.

John.

On Fri, Aug 2, 2024 at 1:16 AM Vincent van Hees <v.va...@accelting.com> wrote:

> Thanks for your report. I think this was fixed in June: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues/1160 ?
>
> Could you confirm?
>
> Also, if the issue persist please share a reproducible example such that we can investigate.
>
> Thanks,
>
> Vincent
>
> On Monday, 22 July 2024 at 10:46 PM, Jiaxin “Grace” Chen <rusc...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear colleagues,
> >
> > When processing our actigraphy data using GGIR, we noticed that a number of raw data files (about 15 out of 155) generated an error message during Part 4:
> > "Error in if (is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero”
> >
> > After some investigation, we traced the error message back to function g.sib.det(). See below our processes and proposed solution:
> > The printed error message occurred in line 297 in g.part4.R
> > The issue is from the variable defaultGuiderOnset having a NULL value (which results in is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE to have length 0).
> > To find out why the variable defaultGuiderOnset is NULL, we noted that it takes its value from SPTE_start[j], as assigned on line 292.
> > SPTE_start came from the meta.sleep.folder, which contains RData outputs generated by function g.part3().
> > We compared the milestone 3 files from data files that ran successfully and files that failed and observed that in the data frame "sib.cla.sum," files that failed contained the value 0 in the night variable, while files that ran to completion had night indexes starting at 1.
> > We looked at the g.part3.R file to find out where the values for the variable night were generated.
> > The data frame "sib.cla.sum" is created by the function g.sib.sum() in line 118, and this function requires an input parameter "SLE."
> > SLE was generated using the function g.sib.det() in line 82.
> > From here, we looked at g.sib.det.R.
> > The variable night is initialized in line 116 to contain the value of 0.
> > These values were later modified according to another variable, sptei, which was initialized as 0 in line 221.
> > We believe the problem lies in lines 230 and 231, where nights containing data under 60 epochs were skipped, and the sptei was not updated in the next line (i.e., at this point, for these nights, sptei == 0).
> > It follows that, for nights under 60 epochs, the variable night will have a value of 0.
> > So, in g.part4.R, when the defaultGuiderOnset variable is set to SPTE_start[j], where “j” is the location index in the list nnights.list (line 265) and that a location index of 0 will result in NULL values, we know the following:
> > min(sib.cla.sum$night) == 0, for these problematic files
> > (lines 216-217) first_night = min(sib.cla.sum$night)
> > last_night = max(sib.cla.sum$night)
> > (line 219) nnightlist = first_night:last_night
> > (line 226) nnights.list = nnightlist
> > Since “j” will be of value 0 in the first iteration of the for-loop starting at line 265, we will see SPTE_start[j] == NULL, and consequently, defaultGuiderOnset == NULL.
> > In our specific cases, we can address this issue by running GGIR() separately for input data files that crashed due to this error by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()). However, for replicability purposes, it is not ideal that these input files will be run using a slightly different shell script than the rest of the inputs.
> >
> > We wanted to share these with the rest of the GGIR community in case anyone else has run into a similar issue. If helpful, we would also like to propose a potential fix in the source code so that this won't be an issue for future projects:

Note that metadatadir is not a parameter you can use in a GGIR-call, it is only used internally by GGIR itself. It is important that you provide outputdir and datadir consistently, because only then GGIR knows where to find the milestone data it previously generated.

When you use GGIR() with mode =1:5 you also will get the part 1 output. I do not understand why you would want to split the function. You now risk using inconsistent parameters values between the two GGIR calls, which will confuse GGIR and may lead to unexpected behaviour.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR Cut Points - Excluding Light or Vigorous Activity
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] GGIR Cut Points - Excluding Light or Vigorous Activity
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ariel,

GGIR always calculates all intensity levels based on the assumption that humans consume energy on a continuous scale. We are not robots who either off (inactive) or on (moderately or vigorously active). I think you misunderstood the publications: The fact that they did not propose thresholds (cut-points) for all levels does not mean those levels do not exist, it is just that the authors did not have the data to justify proposing those thresholds.

I see two options:
Explore what might be a reasonable threshold value based on the thresholds you find for other/similar populations. For example, in a slightly younger or older age group? Next, interpret the estimates for that threshold carefully.
Give threshold.lig the same value as threshold.mod, which will then result in 0 minutes spent in light PA. Similarly, if you specify threshold.vig = Inf you should get zero minutes spent in vigorous PA. However, I think you will then have to acknowledge in your reporting that inactivity in your results equals light and inactivity combined and moderate equals moderate and vigorous combined.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] unbouted + bouted not equalling total
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chloe,

Parameter bout.metric was deprecated several years ago, so you can ignore it. GGIR only has one bout detection algorithm and this comes with a variety of parameters (bout duration, bout threshold, and the criteria on the fraction of time that needs to meet the threshold criteria).

Total inactivity time represents the total number of epochs that individually meet the threshold criteria for inactivity.

When summing up the individual inactivity behaviours (bouts, unbouted) please be aware that:
If boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> is not 1 then inactivity bouts may include small gaps representing activity behaviours that are counted as inactivity because they are part of inactivity bouts. However, these epochs are not part of total inactivity time even though they are counted towards time in the inactivity bouts.
If boutcriter.lig or boutcriter.mvpa is not 1 then LIPA or MVPA bouts may include small gaps representing inactive behaviour that is counted towards those bouts. However, these epochs are counted towards total inactivity time.

As a result dur_day_total_IN_min and the sum of the individual class are not identical and provide complementary information. The first one ignores the whole concept of bouts and assesses each epoch individually while the second approach sticks with the bout detection approach.

Kind regards,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Question Using Config File
messages.body_plain:
Dear Reagan,

I just noticed I did not reply to your message from August. You have two options:
Specify all your non-default parameters via the GGIR function call in your R script, including parameter loglocation, but do not fiddle with config.csv because config.csv is just a log of how GGIR combines your function arguments, its internal defaults and the information in the previous GGIR function run. Any parameter specified in your R script will overrule whatever is specified in the config.csv and after the analysis the value will be overwritten in the config.csv file.
Only use the config.csv file, for example if you want to replicate a previous analysis.  Here, you will have to specify file paths such as datadir and outputdir via the GGIR function call but all other parameters no longer need to be specified.

For details see: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter2_Pipeline.html#configuration-file-

Thanks,

Vincent

Hi there,

I am using GGIR to process raw accelerometer data collected from ActiGraph GT3X+ devices. However, it takes approximately 17 minutes to process data for one participant, which is significantly longer than the 3–10 minutes mentioned in the tutorial.

For replication purposes, I have attached the following files: the configuration file, R code, and R log ('Experiment_rawacc_log.txt). As the file size exceeds the upload limit, the zipped raw data for one participant has been stored here (https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/pax_g/62161.tar.bz2).

Your suggestions would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,
Dave

messages.body_plain:
Hi Dave,

Regarding speed:

>  which is significantly longer than the 3–10 minutes mentioned in the tutorial.

The time indicated is derived from standard GGIR use cases. Note that you are not processing standard ActiGraph native .gt3x output but a file format specific to one wave of the NHANES study for which I have never tested GGIR. Please understand that without community efforts I do not have the resources to tailor GGIR to every new data format. If accelerometer manufacturers, organisations that collect data, and/or researchers want GGIR to be compatible with new formats then please help coordinate/fund GGIR updates.

That said, with rmc.unit.time = "POSIX" as you are currently using, GGIR will check <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/blob/master/R/read.myacc.csv.R#L199-L258> whether fractions of seconds are missing from the timestamps. This is a rather slow process. Meanwhile rmc.unit.time = "character" does not do this check and assumes that timestamp format is in line with the value of "rmc.format.time" including fractional seconds, so you may want to try that instead as it will run a lot faster.

If this solves your problem then I would appreciate if you could propose:
Revisions to the GGIR documentation to make this clear to other users with the same challenge.
Expansions to the GGIR documentation to better guide future users of this specific NHANES data format.

Regarding your R script:
I guess your way of appending files is not very memory friendly as it requires that all raw data points from an entire recording fit in memory. Alternatively, you could consider using GGIR parameter maxRecordingInterval https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#maxrecordinginterval This will reduce memory needs as data is first processed per file and then appended at feature (metric) level, which avoids that your computer ever needs to hold all raw data in memory at the same time. Further, you could also try a hybrid solution where you may append 2-3 days of raw data and then process it with maxRecordingInterval. Note that all this will affect auto-calibration procedure and by that will cause (minor) inconsistencies in final values.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

> > > >
> > > > After some investigation, we traced the error message back to function g.sib.det(). See below our processes and proposed solution:
> > > > The printed error message occurred in line 297 in g.part4.R
> > > > The issue is from the variable defaultGuiderOnset having a NULL value (which results in is.na <http://is.na>(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE to have length 0).
> > > > To find out why the variable defaultGuiderOnset is NULL, we noted that it takes its value from SPTE_start[j], as assigned on line 292.

> > > > SLE was generated using the function g.sib.det() in line 82.
> > > > From here, we looked at g.sib.det.R.
> > > > The variable night is initialized in line 116 to contain the value of 0.
> > > > These values were later modified according to another variable, sptei, which was initialized as 0 in line 221.

> > > > last_night = max(sib.cla.sum$night)

> > > > In our specific cases, we can address this issue by running GGIR() separately for input data files that crashed due to this error by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()). messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] part6 output
messages.body_plain:
Thanks Jan for confirming,

Anne - You may need to set overwrite = TRUE and if you have been adding and removing  parameters to your R script consider deleting config.csv to avoid that previously specified non-default parameter values affect your analysis as discussed here: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter2_Pipeline.html#parameter-extraction-order.

Part 6 output parameters are not documented in https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRoutput.html yet, it is on my to do list. However, I hope that most variables names are clear from the discussion in https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter13_CircadianRhythm.html

Regarding difference between part 2 and 6:
Part 2 circadian rhythm analysis tries to use every valid data point in the recording. This is not ideal as it also can reflect incomplete days which makes it inconsistent with other parts of GGIR where we are more strict about inclusion/exclusion of valid days. It is not by definition wrong, but when comparing physical activity estimates with CR estimates it kind of helps to know that the same part of the time series was used.
Part 6 focuses on the time window as specified with parameter part6Window to help align with the subsegment of the recording as used for part 5 analysis, and it omits days that are considered invalid.
Sorry, I now see indeed that this was not part of the documentation. I will add this.

Thanks,

Vincent

If anyone has come across this before, how did you treat this data - i.e., did you use or disregard the data?

Gareth

messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Thank you for this great package. I am using it for the first time to analyse ActiGraph GT3X hip-worn data (not worn during sleep) and have a few questions.

1. For several participants I seem to get different valid days in different csv files. For example, for one participant, part2_daysummary provides data for 7 valid days as does part5_daysummary_full (from the QC folder) but part5_daysummary WW (not from the QC folder) provides only 4 valid days.

Is there a potential reason for discrepancies in valid data from the GGIR outputs?

2. To my understanding, time in MVPA differs between part 2 and part 5 due to when MVPA can happen and differences in overlapping with midnight.

Is this correct?

3. When I compare time spent in intensities between the file summary report (colour shadings) and part5_daysummary_full (from the QC folder) they don't always correspond, i.e., the amount of shading doesn't always correspond with the values for LIPA or MVPA in the csv file.

Could there be a reason for this?

4. Lastly, the file for this participant and others have a calibration error of 0.006 or 0.007 despite the fact that the file isn't corrupt nor too short. The QC message reads " re-calibration attempted with all available data, but possibly not good enough: Check calibration error variable to verify this". I have tried to use the auto calibration command but it seems that the collaboration error is too high to be fixed by this.

Any suggestions for how to deal with calibration errors higher than 0.005?

Attached is the R script that I used.

Really appreciate any feedback received,

Kind regards,
Callum

messages.body_plain:
Hi Gareth,

What does part2_summary.csv column calib_status say? In my memory the value for that column is always stored and should clarify why calibration error was not estimated. For example, auto-calibration may be skipped if not enough data is available for the algorithm, which typically happens when the sensor is hardly worn.

Note that file QC/data_quality_report.csv also has the calibration error estimates and status

If the GGIR output indicates that the sensor was worn for an acceptable amount of time (multiple days) then you may want to consider reprocessing the same file using the calibration coefficients derived by GGIR in a different recording with the same device ID. For this you can use parameter backup.cal.coef: https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html#backup-cal-coef

Best,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Hi Callum,

Yes, this is intentional. Each part of GGIR has its own definition of a day and criteria to define a valid day and that is why GGIR has all these parts. To understand this you would have to read the documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/index.html. In short: part 2 is calendar day oriented (midnight-midnight), part 4 night-oriented defined from noon-noon or 6pm-6pm, part 5 can facilitate wakeup-wakeup next day.
See documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/chapter12_TimeUseAnalysis.html#seemingly-overlapping-variables-between-ggir-part-2-and-part-5-output
See documentation https://wadpac.github.io/GGIR/articles/GGIRParameters.html?q=visualreport#visualreport The file summary report is known to be inaccurate as it was never intended for quality checking data when I first created it. On a positive note I will replace it in the next release with a visual report that is intended for quality checking data.
I think 0.005 is not too bad, and in studies I have worked on we typically only excluded recordings with more than 0.01 estimated error. However, my response to Gareth <https://groups.google.com/g/RpackageGGIR/c/aiShv3Sb3o4/m/NnF0YbjxDgAJ> a couple of minutes ago may be of interest to you.

Best,

Vincent
